items.stem: Your LLM feature's cost is dominated by many repeated, identical prompts (same FAQ asked constantly). Which architectural change cuts cost most directly?

options.text: Add a cache keyed on the prompt so identical requests return a stored response without calling the model
options.rationale: Correct: caching avoids paying for repeated identical generations.

options.text: Switch every request to the largest model
options.rationale: A bigger model raises cost; it does not avoid repeated calls.
Context size does not reduce repeated identical calls.
Streaming affects perceived latency, not repeated-call cost.

items.explanation: Correct: caching avoids paying for repeated identical generations.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques reduce the cost or latency of an LLM application? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Routing easy requests to a smaller, cheaper model
options.rationale: Correct: model routing matches request difficulty to model cost.

options.text: Caching responses for repeated identical inputs
Always sending the full conversation history on every call
options.rationale: Resending everything increases tokens, cost and latency.

options.text: Adding more tools to every request
options.rationale: Extra tool definitions add tokens and do not reduce cost.

items.explanation: Correct: model routing matches request difficulty to model cost.

items.stem: Why design explicit timeouts and fallbacks around model provider calls?

options.text: The provider can be slow, rate-limited or down, and the app must degrade gracefully instead of hanging or erroring
options.rationale: Correct: external dependencies fail, so the architecture must handle it.

options.text: Because the model is always deterministic
options.rationale: Determinism is unrelated and not generally true.
Timeouts are unrelated to whether retrieval is used.

options.text: Because fallbacks remove the need for the model
options.rationale: Fallbacks handle failure; they do not replace the model.

items.explanation: Correct: external dependencies fail, so the architecture must handle it.
